newsitem.title: USA: U.S. wetlands program to aid Florida lake project.
newsitem.headline: U.S. wetlands program to aid Florida lake project.

text.p: A federal wetlands program will provide $26 million to restore up to 13,000 acres of land as part of a project to clean up Lake Apopka in northern Florida, the Agriculture Department said Wednesday.
The goal of the project was to make Lake Apopka, near Orlando, fit for swimming and fishing, it said.
Funds from the Wetlands Reserve Program would be used to restore wetlands along the lake's north shoreline that were drained during the 1940s for use in growing vegetables.

In a statement, the department said the wetlands project was the culmination of a long-term restoration program by the St Johns River Water Management District. Wetlands restoration was intended to reduce agricultural runoff, mainly phosphorus, into the lake.
"This (wetland restoration) is a project that the farmers came to us with," said a water district spokeswoman, adding that acquisition negotiations were under way.
Two birds on the federal endangered species list, the wood stork and the whooping crane, were expected to benefit from the restoration, which would create habitat for wading and migratory birds.
